canonical_name: JaxUED -- JaxUED: A simple and useable UED library in Jax (Samuel Coward and Michael Beukman and Jakob Foerster; no institution named in README, pyproject author email domain robots.ox.ac.uk; 2024-2025)
aliases: JAXUED_TEST (default wandb project name in examples)
lineage: README: 'similar goals to CleanRL'; inspirations listed under See Also: Minimax (facebookresearch/minimax: 'UED baselines, with support for multi-gpu training, and more parallel versions of PLR/ACCEL'), PureJaxRL, JaxIRL, Mava, JaxMARL, Gymnax, Jumanji, Pgx, Brax, XLand-MiniGrid, Craftax. docs/maze_dr.md: 'It follows the PureJaxRL-style training loop.' docs/maze.md: maze 'based on Minigrid'. Source comments credit minimax for utils.py (ued_scores) and make_level_mutator_minimax. Downstream per README 'Projects using JaxUED': Craftax, ReMiDi. || main loop (reader, from the code): In examples/maze_plr.py, train_step (jax.lax.scan-ned eval_freq times inside train_and_eval_step, itself looped num_updates//eval_freq times in main) draws a replay decision from the LevelSampler (or, with --use_accel, uses the previous update_state to force a mutate step after each replay step) and jax.lax.switch-es into one of on_new_levels (sample random mazes, roll out the PPO-LSTM agent, score trajectories with MaxMC or positive value loss, insert_batch into the buffer, update the policy only if exploratory_grad_updates), on_replay_levels (sample_replay_levels weighted by rank-score and staleness, roll out, update_batch scores, always update the policy) or on_mutate_levels (mutate the last replayed batch with make_level_mutator_minimax, roll out, score and insert the children).

human_capability_summary.built_to: Provide CleanRL-style single-file, understandable JAX reference implementations of common Unsupervised Environment Design methods (DR, PLR, ACCEL, PAIRED) plus a LevelSampler, an UnderspecifiedEnv interface and a Maze environment, for researchers to modify and prototype on.
human_capability_summary.pressure: README: existing UED code hides implementation details behind abstraction; JaxUED is 'primarily intended for researchers looking to get in the weeds of UED algorithm development' with 'minimal dependency implementations' that 'expose all implementation details' and facilitate 'easy, rapid prototyping of new ideas'.
human_capability_summary.success_means: README states no quantitative criterion; the scripts log solve rates and returns on fixed held-out eval mazes (SixteenRooms, Labyrinth, StandardMaze variants) every eval_freq updates plus level-sampler statistics, and eval mode writes cum_rewards and episode_lengths per level.
